● He participates in club activities after he’s done with classes every Wednesday.
● After he’s done with classes every Wednesday, he participates in club activities.
● I want to buy a new car because my car is old.
● Because my car is old, I want to buy a new car.
● Kate cries whenever she misses her mother.
● Whenever Kate misses her mother, she cries.

3
Adverb Clause
● Place – wherever, anywhere, everywhere, where
Example: Everywhere she goes, she brings a camera.
● Time – since, while, as soon as, before, after, until, when, anytime
Example: While we were waiting for the pizza guy to arrive, we played poker at the kitchen table.
● Reason – because, since, as, for, so that
Example: Because it was exceptionally cold, I wore my winter jacket.
● Condition – if, when, unless, even if, even though
Example: Even if they lose by five goals, people will still love them.
● Contrast – though, although, despite, in spite of, whereas
Example: Despite the poor service provided by the wait staff, we still enjoyed the food and the
atmosphere of the restaurant.

4
Adverb Clause Paraphrasing Sample
Reason – because, since, as, for, so that
Example: Because it was exceptionally cold, I wore my winter jacket.
=> I wore my winter jacket because it was exceptionally cold.
=> I wore my winter jacket since it was exceptionally cold.
=> I put on my winter coat since the weather was frigid.
Try: He participates in club activities after he’s done with classes every weekend.

Subordinating Conjunctions Usage
1⃣If → If you study hard, you will pass the exam. (Condition)
2⃣Since → Since it was raining, we stayed inside. (Cause & Effect)
3⃣As → She smiled as she walked into the room. (Manner)
4⃣When → Call me when you arrive at the airport. (Time)
5⃣Although → Although he was tired, he finished his homework. (Contrast)
6⃣While → She listened to music while she was working. (Time/Simultaneous Action)
7⃣After → We went to dinner after the movie ended. (Time)
8⃣Before → Finish your homework before you go outside. (Time)
9⃣Until → We waited at the café until the rain stopped. (Time)
Because → She was late because her car broke down. (Cause & Effect)

ADJECTIVE CLAUSE (DESCRIBING THE PIZZA)
 SUBJECT, VERB, CONNECTOR, SUBJECT, VERB
We ate the pizza that the teacher recommended.
ADJECTIVE CLAUSE (DESCRIBING THE PIZZA)

The pizza that the teacher recommended was delicious.
NOTE: The adjective clause connector is often omitted in spoken English and informal writing.

Adjective Clause Paraphrasing Sample
My boss, who just bought a new car, is very rich.
My manager, who recently purchased a new vehicle, is quite wealthy. << too similar
=> It was my wealthy boss who recently purchased the new car.
I ate at a cheap restaurant with my friend, James, yesterday.
=> James, who is my friend, and I had some food at an affordable eatery yesterday.
=> Yesterday, I had a meal at a cheap restaurant with my friend whose name is
James.

Noun Clause
● Can be used as a subject: What I need is my own room.
● Can be used as a predicate nominative: The most important lesson I've learned is how
to forgive.
● A direct object: He knows what happened yesterday.
● An indirect object: We will give whoever wins the contest a prize.
● An object of a preposition: She is interested in what you have to say.
